diagnosis: All four rollouts passed without accessing any of the decisive facts (PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4). This indicates that the model is defaulting to common practices and general guidelines, such as setting maximum concurrent connections to 10,000, using a 5-second retry interval, and handling data processing in the primary region with 90-day retention. These defaults do not require the specific hidden information provided by PF1, PF2, PF3, and PF4.

fix_instructions: Tighten the checks C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9, and C10 to require more specific and less generic values. For example, set C1 to require excluding specific account IDs (e.g., acct-204, acct-219, etc.), C2 to specify a precise connection limit (e.g., 6,000), and C3 to mandate a unique retry interval (e.g., 30 seconds). Ensure each check depends on the corresponding decisive fact (PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4) to prevent the model from relying on default settings.
